A Comparative Analysis of Cloudflare, AWS WAF, Akamai, DataDome, and CAPTCHAs

In this article, we analyze common HTTP headers and DOM markers emitted by various security products.

Cloudflare & WAF

Cloudflare reverse proxy nodes often attach headers such as cf-ray: 8e5f123456789abc-IAD and cf-mitigated: challenge when challenge mode is activated. In client HTML, you might see container classes like cf-turnstile or error wrappers like cf-error-details.

AWS WAF & CloudFront

AWS CloudFront assigns request IDs via x-amz-cf-id. When AWS WAF inspects traffic, it can issue an aws-waf-token cookie or respond with 405 Method Not Allowed. Integration usually involves the AWS WAF SDK marker aws-waf-.

DataDome & Akamai

DataDome uses tracking scripts like js.datadome.co/tags.js and sets x-datadome: protected. Akamai GHost edge servers attach x-akamai-transformed and error pages containing Reference #18.12345678.1234567890.abcdef12. Bot Manager uses cookies like _abck.

reCAPTCHA, hCaptcha, and Arkose MatchKey

Google reCAPTCHA v2 uses g-recaptcha widgets, hCaptcha uses h-captcha, and Arkose Labs uses arkose-enforcement containers with callback functions like setupArkose(). 


      // Example configuration snippet (not executed)
